primary_work.title: On the Identifiability of Causal Abstractions
primary_work.official_code: not located in primary records or targeted searches

established_boundary: Under the audited weakly supervised paired-observation assumptions, the unknown intervention family identifies a quotient causal graph induced by the partition P(sigma(nd(I*))); language that only names or is generated from this quotient cannot identify a finer microscopic intervention-target partition.
decision: NARROWED TO LANGUAGE-BASED STRICT REFINEMENT BEYOND THE INTERVENTION-INDUCED MAXIMAL CAUSAL ABSTRACTION — NOT ADOPTED
rejected_claims: coarse target grouping under unknown multi-node interventions is itself a novel language contribution
language recovering or naming the intervention-induced quotient proves finer target-partition identifiability
task success, next-state prediction, paraphrase consistency, or shuffle degradation establish refinement beyond the identifiable quotient
necessary_condition: I(P_residual; L | A(X,X_tilde)) > 0 for the residual partition after non-language quotienting, plus an externally fixed anti-recoding anchor; the information condition alone is not sufficient.
remaining_rq: After quotienting by the finest causal abstraction identifiable from the available unknown intervention family, can an externally anchored population language channel strictly refine a residual quotient block and jointly identify raw-utterance equivalence classes with the refined intervention-target partition while ruling out joint recoding?
